headline: Coinbase and Strategy report third-quarter results after the US close tonight, and the prediction market Polymarket paused trading after an exploit that took more than $2.5M.

stories.title: Coinbase and Strategy report third-quarter results after the US close tonight
stories.summary: Coinbase and Strategy report after the 4pm ET close on Thursday (03:00 Friday Bangkok). Analysts expect Coinbase to post a loss.
points: Coinbase's live Q&A is at 2:00pm PT (5:00pm ET, 04:00 Friday Bangkok); Strategy's webinar is at 5:00pm ET, per the companies.

Analysts expect Coinbase to lose about $0.22 a share on about $1.20B of revenue, per 24/7 Wall St; a year ago it earned $1.44 a share on $1.87B. Coinbase has missed revenue estimates three quarters in a row.

Wall Street is split on trading: forecasts for Coinbase's quarterly trading volume range from $141B (Oppenheimer) to $173B (JPMorgan), per CoinDesk. Robinhood's crypto revenue fell 55% from a year earlier.
Strategy already reported a $20.91B unaudited gain on its bitcoin for the quarter in a filing, and held 848,517 BTC on 18 Oct, per PrimeXBT.

stories.title: Polymarket pauses trading after a wallet-drain exploit of about $2.65M
stories.summary: The prediction market Polymarket switched its exchange to cancel-only mode after an exploit. It blamed a compromised third-party provider and said it had found and fixed the cause.
points: A suspected attacker wallet held about $2.65M in POL after swapping USDC.e, per Arkham data cited by The Block; the funds were then moved on.
Polymarket referred the case to law enforcement. It has not named the provider or said whether users will be repaid, per The Block.
Cancel-only mode means users can cancel open orders but cannot place new ones.

Separately, Utah has filed 14 criminal counts against rival Kalshi and its co-founders over online gambling; the CFTC has sued Utah, saying only federal regulators oversee these contracts, per CoinDesk.

stories.title: NYSE owner ICE moves to bring Hyperliquid-style perpetual futures to the US
stories.summary: Intercontinental Exchange, which owns the New York Stock Exchange, will partner with and invest in TradeXYZ to offer perpetual futures built on Hyperliquid's technology, per The Block. The plan still needs regulatory approval and has no launch date.
points: The markets would cover crypto, stocks, stock indices, commodities and currencies, with ICE running the regulated exchange and clearing, per The Block.
Hyperliquid's HYPE token rose about 15% to around $91.21 on the news; its all-time high is $97.96, per The Block (at 10:43am ET Thursday).
CFTC staff opened a US path for perpetual futures with an advisory and no-action relief in May, per The Block.
